page.layout: One page of text in one column. Running head at top, with page number 489 at top right. Text from the previous page continues at the top. Centred chapter number LXXI. Signature "Hh 5" at the foot. No marginal notes.

p.i: Iovam Deum vestrum non jam vobis istas omnes nationes expulsurum esse. Sed eas vobis fore tanq̄ decipulam quandam & obicem, & laterum stimulum, & oculos spinas, eosq;, ut auferamini ex hac tam bona terra, vobis à Iova Deo vestro data. Iosu.23.

main_text.p: Aliquanto post, messis tritici tempore Samson visit uxorem suam, caprum ferens, & ad eam admitti se in cubiculū postulat. Sed mulieris pater eum prohibuit, dicens sese, cum eam illi invisam esse putaret, eam ejus familiari locasse: esse tamen ei sororem, ut natu minorem, sic forma venustiorem, eam pro illa duceret.

Tum Samson apud illos præfatus, sese tum non esse Palæstinis injuriam facturum, si eus[?] malum inferret, discedit: captisq; trecentis vulpibus, & earum caudis inter se obversis, singulas faces binis caudis interponit, ijsq; incensis, vulpes in Palæstin. segetes laxat, atque ita & metas, & segetes, & vineas, & oliveta combussit. Hujus facinoris authorem Pa-

page.notes: Running head printed "NVPTIALES." with V for capital U; corrected to NUPTIALES. Page number 489 read from the printed head. Signature "Hh 5" at the foot; the final character is doubtful. "si eus malum" is printed as "eus" in the scan (probably "eis"); left as read and marked. The chapter number LXXI is a bare number, so it is written as a paragraph, not a heading. The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The two Biblical lines and the reference "Iosu.23." stand in the text. "Pa-" is a line-end hyphen; the catchword and continuation are not on this page.
